newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to bump up social security spending - Zedillo.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to bump up social security spending - Zedillo.

text.p: The Mexican government will increase its contributions to the Social Security Institute (IMSS) by 700 percent this year, President Ernesto Zedillo said on Wednesday.

"These contributions will increase from 2.641 billion pesos ($338 million) in 1996 to 21.379 billion pesos ($2.737 billion) in 1997, that is, an increase of 700 percent," Zedillo said in a speech to IMSS directors.
Government contributions account for about one-third of the 79.949 billion pesos ($10.236 billion) assigned to the IMSS to treat 37 million people covered by the scheme.
All private sector workers on employers' payrolls have to pay an insurance quota to the IMSS, which covers them and their families for health care.
Zedillo said funds chanelled into social security would help to consolidate reforms to the IMSS.
"With the reforms undertaken in the Institute, now we do have social security for the twenty-first century," he said.
